tweaks.name: Diagnostic data: Required only
tweaks.hint: Limits Windows diagnostic data to the Required level (the lowest level honored on Pro).
tweaks.description: Sets the AllowTelemetry policy to 1 (Required). 'Off/Security' (0) is only honored on Enterprise, Education and Server; on Pro it behaves like Required. Optional diagnostic data and tailored-experience uploads stop. Windows Update keeps working normally.

evidence.notes: Value 0 is treated as on (equivalent to Required on Pro).

tweaks.name: Connected User Experiences and Telemetry service off
tweaks.hint: Disables the DiagTrack service. Negligible performance effect (measure if curious); may break some Insider/feedback features.
tweaks.description: Sets the DiagTrack service (Connected User Experiences and Telemetry) to Disabled and stops it. This also stops Required diagnostic data uploads, which Microsoft uses for update quality and safeguard holds. Separated from the Required-level policy because it goes beyond what Microsoft supports on Pro. Measured CPU use of DiagTrack is negligible.

evidence.notes: Microsoft lists DiagTrack as safe to disable on Windows Server with Desktop Experience; not part of any preset.

tweaks.name: Ads, tips and suggestions off
tweaks.hint: Turns off the advertising ID, tailored experiences, Settings/Start suggestions and tip notifications.
tweaks.description: Sets the documented policies for the advertising ID, diagnostic-data-based tailored experiences and online tips in Settings, and turns off the per-user 'suggested content' toggles for Settings, Start and tip notifications. Removes promotional content and the background content downloads that feed it.

evidence.notes: ContentDeliveryManager and Start_IrisRecommendations are the per-user values behind the Settings toggles.

tweaks.name: Widgets off
tweaks.hint: Turns off the Widgets board and its news feed (no background feed refresh, no taskbar weather button).
tweaks.description: Sets the AllowNewsAndInterests policy to 0. Removes the Widgets board, the taskbar widget button and the background processes that refresh the feed.

evidence.notes: Documented policy, supported on Pro.

tweaks.name: Microsoft Edge background activity off
tweaks.hint: Stops Edge from preloading at sign-in (Startup Boost) and from running in the background after you close it.
tweaks.description: Sets the Edge policies StartupBoostEnabled and BackgroundModeEnabled to 0. Edge no longer keeps processes running at sign-in or after its last window closes, freeing memory and CPU while you play. Edge itself keeps working; it starts slightly slower.

evidence.notes: Edge shows 'Your browser is managed by your organization' while policies are set.

tweaks.name: Windows Update active hours 10:00-04:00
tweaks.hint: No automatic update restarts between 10:00 and 04:00 (18 h, the maximum). Updates still install; never disables updates.
tweaks.description: Sets the documented active-hours policy (SetActiveHours = 1, start 10, end 4). Windows will not restart automatically for updates inside this window, protecting evening matches. Replaces the often-recommended NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers, which Microsoft says does not work as described and can block quality-update reboots entirely.

evidence.notes: Maximum active-hours range is 18 hours. Settings shows active hours as managed while the policy is set.

tweaks.name: Keep my drivers (no driver updates via Windows Update)
tweaks.hint: Stops Windows Update from replacing drivers (e.g. your NVIDIA driver). Update GPU, chipset and NIC drivers yourself.
tweaks.description: Sets the ExcludeWUDriversInQualityUpdate policy to 1. Windows Update stops offering driver updates, so a newer or older OEM driver never silently replaces the NVIDIA driver you installed. Trade-off: you must update GPU, chipset, LAN and Bluetooth drivers yourself, including security fixes.

evidence.notes: Affects all drivers, not only the GPU.

tweaks.name: Background apps off (Store apps)
tweaks.hint: Stops Microsoft Store apps from running in the background. May delay Store-app notifications. Measure before/after.
tweaks.description: Sets the LetAppsRunInBackground policy to 2 (force deny). Packaged (Store) apps can no longer run background tasks; classic desktop programs such as Discord or Steam are not affected. Notifications from Store apps (Mail, Phone Link, Xbox) may arrive late. The gain is usually small; measure before/after.

evidence.notes: Situational trade-off.

tweaks.name: Reduce animations and transparency
tweaks.hint: Turns off window animations, taskbar animations and transparency. Snappier UI, not more FPS. Measure if in doubt.
tweaks.description: Sets EnableTransparency = 0, MinAnimate = "0" and TaskbarAnimations = 0. Windows and the taskbar feel more immediate and the compositor does slightly less work on the desktop. In-game FPS does not change; measure if you want proof. Sign out to apply fully.

evidence.notes: UI responsiveness preference.

tweaks.name: AI features off (Recall, Click to Do, Paint AI)
tweaks.hint: Applies Microsoft's documented policies to disable Recall, Click to Do and Paint's generative AI features.
tweaks.description: Sets AllowRecallEnablement = 0 (Recall unavailable; its bits are removed), DisableAIDataAnalysis = 1 (no snapshots), DisableClickToDo = 1 and the Paint Cocreator, Generative fill and Image Creator policies. Recall exists only on Copilot+ PCs, so on this hardware those values have no visible effect. The Microsoft Copilot app has no supported removal policy on Pro; uninstall it from Settings > Apps if you do not want it.

evidence.notes: DisableClickToDo is listed for Insider builds; TurnOffWindowsCopilot is deprecated and not used; RemoveMicrosoftCopilotApp is not supported on Pro.

tweaks.name: SysMain (Superfetch) off
tweaks.hint: Disables memory prefetching. Negligible on NVMe with 32 GB RAM; may slow app launches slightly. Measure before/after.
tweaks.description: Sets the SysMain service to Disabled and stops it. SysMain preloads frequently used programs into memory; on a fast NVMe SSD with plenty of RAM its benefit and its cost are both small. Honest expectation: no FPS change. Measure load times before/after if you try it.

evidence.notes: Situational; not part of any preset.

tweaks.name: Windows Search indexing off
tweaks.hint: Disables the search indexer. Start/File Explorer/Outlook search become slower. Negligible gain on NVMe; measure.
tweaks.description: Sets the Windows Search service (WSearch) to Disabled and stops it. The indexer already backs off while you are active, so the gaming benefit is usually negligible on NVMe; the cost is slower file and Start menu search. Measure before/after.

evidence.notes: Situational; not part of any preset.

tweaks.name: Microsoft telemetry and CEIP scheduled tasks off
tweaks.hint: Disables Microsoft telemetry/CEIP tasks (Appraiser, CEIP, disk diagnostics, feedback). Small background saving; measure.
tweaks.description: Disables the Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser, Customer Experience Improvement Program, Autochk proxy, disk diagnostic data collector and Feedback (SIUF) scheduled tasks. They collect compatibility and usage data in the background; the Appraiser can use CPU and disk for minutes. Tasks are disabled, never deleted, and missing ones are skipped. Revert re-enables them.

evidence.notes: Microsoft documents CEIP as retired and the Appraiser as a telemetry component; the performance effect is situational, so measure.

tweaks.name: Defer feature updates by 90 days
tweaks.hint: Feature updates (new Windows versions) arrive 90 days after release. Security (quality) updates are never deferred.
tweaks.description: Sets the Windows Update for Business policy DeferFeatureUpdatesPeriodInDays to 90. New Windows versions arrive after early driver and anti-cheat issues are fixed, while monthly security updates keep installing on time. Settings shows updates as managed by your organization while the policy is set. Revert removes the policy.

evidence.notes: Supported on Pro. Quality updates are intentionally left alone.

tweaks.name: Activity history off
tweaks.hint: Windows stops recording and uploading the apps, files and sites you use (activity history), using the documented policies.
tweaks.description: Sets the Group Policy values PublishUserActivities and UploadUserActivities to 0. Windows no longer stores your activity history locally or sends it to Microsoft. Nothing in Windows 11 depends on the history for gaming or productivity. Turning it off removes both policies. Derived from WinUtil.

evidence.notes: ADMX OSPolicy.admx (PublishUserActivities, UploadUserActivities). Windows default: not configured.

tweaks.attribution: Chris Titus Tech WinUtil (commit d32efeb), MIT License, tweak 'Activity History - Disable'

tweaks.name: Location services off
tweaks.hint: Turns off Windows location for every app and service with the documented policy. Breaks Find my device, auto time zone and local weather.
tweaks.description: Sets the "Turn off location" policy (DisableLocation = 1). No app or Windows feature can read the PC location. Find my device, setting the time zone automatically, maps and local weather or news stop working, which is why this is Advanced and adapted from WinUtil (which also disabled the geolocation service; the policy alone is enough). Turning it off removes the policy.

evidence.notes: ADMX Sensors.admx DisableLocation (machine). Windows default: not configured.

tweaks.sideEffects: Find my device, automatic time zone, Maps and location-based weather, news and search results stop working.
tweaks.attribution: Chris Titus Tech WinUtil (commit d32efeb), MIT License, tweak 'Location Tracking - Disable' (adapted to the documented policy)

tweaks.name: Microsoft consumer experiences off
tweaks.hint: Stops Windows from installing suggested third-party apps and showing Microsoft account promotions. Honored on Enterprise and Education only.
tweaks.description: Sets the "Turn off Microsoft consumer experiences" policy (DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures = 1). Windows then stops auto-installing promoted Store apps and games and stops account-related promotions. Microsoft honors this policy only on Enterprise and Education; on Pro and Home it is shown as not applicable, and the ads and suggestions item covers the per-user part. Turning it off removes the policy. Derived from WinUtil.

evidence.notes: ADMX CloudContent.admx. Policy CSP Experience/AllowWindowsConsumerFeatures lists Enterprise and Education only.

tweaks.attribution: Chris Titus Tech WinUtil (commit d32efeb), MIT License, tweak 'ConsumerFeatures - Disable'

tweaks.name: Bing web results in Start search off
tweaks.hint: Start menu search shows only local apps, files and settings, and stops sending what you type to Bing.
tweaks.description: Sets BingSearchEnabled = 0 for your account, so Windows Search no longer queries Bing as you type in Start. Local results are unchanged and usually appear faster. Microsoft does not document the value (it is Tier B); the documented web-search policies are not honored on every Windows 11 edition. Nothing to measure: it is a privacy preference. Turning it off removes the value. Derived from WinUtil.

evidence.notes: Undocumented per-user value; Windows default: absent (web results on). Nothing to measure: privacy preference.

tweaks.attribution: Chris Titus Tech WinUtil (commit d32efeb), MIT License, toggle 'Start Menu Bing Search'

tweaks.name: No automatic device metadata and companion apps
tweaks.hint: Windows stops downloading device metadata and the vendor companion apps that come with it when you plug in a mouse, headset or keyboard.
tweaks.description: Sets the documented "Prevent device metadata retrieval from the Internet" policy. Plugging in a peripheral no longer pulls vendor software (for example a mouse or RGB suite) through Windows Update; drivers still install, and you can install vendor software yourself. This replaces WinUtil's folder-permission blocks for Razer and Logitech installers with the supported policy. Turning it off removes the policy.

evidence.notes: ADMX DeviceSetup.admx DeviceMetadata_PreventDeviceMetadataFromNetwork. Windows default: not configured.

tweaks.attribution: Chris Titus Tech WinUtil (commit d32efeb), MIT License, tweak 'Prevent Device Companion Apps' (also replaces 'Razer/Logitech Software Auto-Install - Disable')

tweaks.name: PowerShell 7 telemetry off
tweaks.hint: Sets POWERSHELL_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 for the whole PC, the documented opt-out for PowerShell 7 usage data. Windows PowerShell 5.1 sends none.
tweaks.description: Adds the machine environment variable POWERSHELL_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT with value 1, which PowerShell 7 checks at start-up before sending its anonymous start-up telemetry. Windows PowerShell 5.1 is not affected. New PowerShell sessions pick it up after you sign out or restart. Turning it off removes the variable. Derived from WinUtil's telemetry tweak (the only part of it that is not already covered).

evidence.notes: Windows default: variable not set.

tweaks.attribution: Chris Titus Tech WinUtil (commit d32efeb), MIT License, tweak 'Telemetry - Disable' (PowerShell part)

tweaks.name: Defer feature updates by 365 days
tweaks.hint: New Windows versions arrive a year after release (the maximum). Monthly security updates keep installing on time.
tweaks.description: Sets the Windows Update for Business policy DeferFeatureUpdatesPeriodInDays to 365, the security-focused option WinUtil also offers. You keep a supported version longer and skip early feature-update issues; monthly quality updates are not deferred. Check that the version you are on stays in support. Turning it off removes the policy.

evidence.notes: Supported on Pro, Enterprise and Education.

tweaks.attribution: Chris Titus Tech WinUtil (commit d32efeb), MIT License, Updates 'Security Settings' (feature deferral)

tweaks.name: Microsoft Edge privacy policies
tweaks.hint: Edge stops personalizing ads and news from your browsing data, and shows no shopping, Rewards or recommendation pop-ups.
tweaks.description: Sets five documented Microsoft Edge policies: no personalization from browsing data (PersonalizationReportingEnabled), no recommendations and promotional notifications, no shopping assistant, no Microsoft Rewards and no in-browser feedback prompts. Browsing, sync and security features such as SmartScreen are not affected. Edge shows "Your browser is managed by your organization" while policies are set. Turning it off removes the five policies.

evidence.notes: PersonalizationReportingEnabled, ShowRecommendationsEnabled, EdgeShoppingAssistantEnabled, ShowMicrosoftRewards, UserFeedbackAllowed = 0. Not domain-restricted. Windows default: not configured.

tweaks.name: Microsoft 365 Apps diagnostic data off
tweaks.hint: Office sends no client diagnostic data and offers no optional connected experiences. Co-authoring and OneDrive keep working.
tweaks.description: Sets the documented Microsoft 365 Apps privacy policies for your account: client software diagnostic data "Neither" (SendTelemetry = 3) and optional connected experiences disabled (ControllerConnectedServicesEnabled = 2). Microsoft notes that "Neither" limits its ability to diagnose Office problems; required service data is still sent. Core connected experiences such as co-authoring and online storage are not touched. Turning it off removes both policies.

evidence.notes: Registry mapping from the same article. Applies to Microsoft 365 Apps version 1904 and later.

tweaks.sideEffects: Optional Office features such as Bing-powered 3D Maps and online pictures from optional services are unavailable.

tweaks.name: Consumer inbox apps removed
tweaks.hint: Removes News, Weather, Solitaire, Clipchamp, Microsoft 365 Copilot (hub) and Get Help. Revert reinstalls them from the Microsoft Store.
tweaks.description: Removes six consumer apps that come with Windows, for your account and for new user profiles, through the protected app-removal path (Store, App Installer, Xbox identity, Gaming Services, Windows Security and frameworks are never touched). This is the safe part of WinUtil's default app list; Calculator, Clock, Sound Recorder, Sticky Notes and Quick Assist stay. Turning it off re-registers each app or reinstalls it from the Microsoft Store, which needs an internet connection.

evidence.notes: Store ids checked on apps.microsoft.com on 2026-10-21.

tweaks.sideEffects: The apps disappear for every user; reinstalling needs the Microsoft Store and an internet connection.
tweaks.attribution: Chris Titus Tech WinUtil (commit d32efeb), MIT License, preset 'AppxDefault' (adapted to the protected list)
